title: Chambers in a shell
hook: An animal can adjust a hidden balance.

knows: Animals can have structures and life stages that differ from humans.
doesNotKnow: The panels stipulate two chamber states: blue indicates liquid and pale indicates gas. Replacing some liquid with gas changes overall buoyancy. The figure is schematic, omits the siphuncle and does not calculate depth or density.

misconception: The observations in this scenario require a different interpretation.
objective: A nautilus adjusts fluid in its shell chambers. In this simplified comparison, which state contains less chamber liquid?

claims.text: An animal can adjust a hidden balance. A nautilus adjusts fluid in its shell chambers. In this simplified comparison, which state contains less chamber liquid? The panels stipulate two chamber states: blue indicates liquid and pale indicates gas. Replacing some liquid with gas changes overall buoyancy. The figure is schematic, omits the siphuncle and does not calculate depth or density. More liquid; More gas

claims.text: Colored chamber states are invented qualitative illustrations, not observed chamber geometry or buoyancy measurements.
In the toy chamber model, what increases as liquid is removed from a chamber? The stipulated model displays more gas-filled space when chamber liquid decreases.
